---
title: "Software and tools"
---

This is a non-exhaustive list of the software and data types I work with.
For examples please see [my blog](blog.qmd) or [get in touch](mailto:consult@mikerspencer.com) to discuss your support requirements.


* Programming
   * [R](https://cran.r-project.org/): Statistical and programming software
   * [RStudio](https://posit.co/products/open-source/rstudio): Development environment for R
   * Linux and Bash: for scaling and automation
   * [Git](https://git-scm.com/): Version control software (for use with Github, Bitbucket, Gitlab, Codeberg, etc.)
   * [Kate IDE](https://kate-editor.org/en-gb/) a lightweight development environment.
* Spatial and GIS
   * [GRASS](https://grass.osgeo.org/): Geographic information system
   * [QGIS](https://qgis.org/): Geographic information system
* Data storage
   * [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/), [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/), [MySQL](https://www.mysql.com/)
   * [Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/), [Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/) and [partitioned data](https://hive.apache.org/)
* Other
   * [Scribus](https://www.scribus.net/): Desktop publishing
   * [Logseq](https://logseq.com/): personal knowledge management - easy notetaking and information retrieval.
   * [https://keepassxc.org/](KeePassXC): password management

My operating system of choice is [Fedora](https://fedoraproject.org/), which is built on Linux.
A lot of the software on this page is also available for Windows and Macs.
I switched from using Windows to Linux in early 2011 and have not regretted the decision.

I've a [help wiki](https://github.com/mikerspencer/help/wiki) of resources I find useful.
Hopefully you find them useful too!

Some of the software listed above have great communities, here are those I work with:

* [EdinbR](http://edinbr.org/) a meetup for users of R
* [OSGeo:UK](https://uk.osgeo.org/) is an umbrella organisation for spatial software
* [PyData Edinburgh](https://www.meetup.com/pydata-edinburgh/) a meetup for users of Python
